symptom: On MPR v2, `describe microflow` of one flow opened 393 of a blank app's 394 unit files (counted by atime), and the next listing after any write opened them all again; wall time is fine on a small app, the cost is per file open and scales with the project
cause: `buildUnitCache` learnt each unit's `$Type` by `os.ReadFile` of its .mxunit and threw the bytes away, because the v2 Unit table has no type column; `InvalidateCache` (every write) dropped the whole cache, and nothing persisted between processes. The `listUnitTypes` doc comment claimed an index that did not exist
insight: Key the type index by ContentsHash, not by unit ID: a content-addressed entry can never be stale, so the index needs no invalidation and survives writes, re-types in place (#503) and other processes; every v2 writer, ours included (`writer_core.go`), keeps the hash in step with the file. The v1 counterpart (`reader_units_v1.go`) keys by blob length for the same reason. Persist on a reader's first rebuild and on Close, not after every write-triggered rebuild, or a 200-statement script rewrites the index 200 times. Measure with `strace -f -e trace=openat` counting distinct .mxunit paths, not wall time: on pedapp (375 files) 375 -> 117, and the remaining 117 are per-type reads the describe really makes (folders for the path, every microflow to find one by name), which is a different cost
